recipes.name: Washed Flour Seitan
instructions: Mix the flour and water to form a dough.
Knead the dough for 8 to 10 minutes.
Rest the dough in water for at least 1 hour (or ideally up to 2 hours). This helps fully hydrate the flour and strengthens the gluten.
Drain and add fresh water. Gently squeeze and stretch the dough in the water for 3 to 5 minutes to begin washing out the starch*.
Drain and repeat washing with fresh water until the water is fairly clear, about 4 to 5 cycles. The dough will shrink and become stretchy and slightly rubbery**.
Let the dough rest in an empty bowl for at least 20 to 30 minutes. It will release water as it rests.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Cook the onion, carrot, celery, and garlic until golden.
Add the remaining broth ingredients and bring to a gentle simmer.
To braid the seitan, leave an inch (2 cm) of the dough intact at one end. Cut two parallel slits along the length of the dough, then braid the three sections.
Pull the braid slightly to stretch the dough and wrap it into a knot.

Place the seitan knot into the simmering broth. Partially cover the pot with the lid, and cook for 1 hour. If the seitan isn't fully submerged, turn the seitan once or twice during the cooking process.
Remove the seitan from the broth and strain out the solids from the broth***.
Store the seitan, as is, in the broth liquid, or shred into bite-sized pieces before storing.
Drain before using in your favourite recipes. Enjoy!

page_recipe_notes: Notes † For best results, use a high-protein white bread flour (ideally 12.5 to 14% protein). All-purpose flour can work, but may yield a softer dough that’s more prone to breaking during washing. † White miso, also called "Shiro Miso," is fermented for less time than red miso, which gives it a milder, sweeter flavour. If substituting red miso, use a smaller amount and adjust to taste, as red miso is saltier and stronger. * Be gentle at first. Aggressive kneading can cause the dough to break apart before the gluten network is strong enough ** If the dough starts to fall apart, let it rest for 10 to 15 minutes to strengthen, then continue washing more gently. *** Tip: use the leftover broth and strained veggies in a soup!

Storage Store the seitan, submerged in broth in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 1 week. The seitan can also be stored in the freezer, with or without the broth. Without the broth, it can be kept for up to a month. With the broth, it can be stored for 2 months. The broth will expand slightly during freezing, so be sure to use a suitable storage container.
